distinguishing_features: Passive high-conductivity annular insert positioned at the ceramic-metal junction
Insert bonded to both the ceramic substrate and metal flange to provide lateral heat conduction
Reduction of local junction temperature gradients rather than deliberate thermal-shock loading
Acoustic-emission and strain-gauge validation of thermal-cycle cracking
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce interfacial thermoelastic stress and crack initiation caused by differential thermal expansion of a constrained ceramic-metal joint during temperature cycling.
parsed.viable_reason: A heat spreader can reduce spatial temperature nonuniformity but does not reduce the bulk temperature excursion driving differential expansion, and a bonded high-conductivity insert can add parallel stiffness and potentially increase joint stress.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Applying a conductive heat spreader to reduce local thermal gradients in a CTE-mismatched joint is a routine thermal-management step that a skilled engineer could derive from the disclosed interfacial-stress physics.
